dash.title: A dash is not zero
dash.body: It means the page does not have data strong enough to support a claim for this scope or point in time.

live.title: A “live” badge in a past reading is deliberate
live.body: Some controls describe the policy currently deployed. They do not claim to reconstruct an older policy.

scope.title: A global signal stays global
scope.body: If a measurement cannot be attributed to an agent, the filter does not turn it into an individual measurement.

refresh.title: Blocks may update in two stages
refresh.body: After a period or time change, the fleet total may arrive before the heavier analyses. Previous values remain visible during the handover.

decisions.title: When to open another page
decisions.lead: Overview provides direction. Specialist pages explain the cause and carry the actions.

quality.title: Quality or a control is deteriorating
quality.body: Open AI Quality to review the results, evaluations, and affected controls.

risk.title: A risk or anomaly appears
risk.body: Open Incidents & procedures to understand the case and the planned response.

release.title: The version appears to have introduced a failure
release.body: Open Release control to review the verdict before exposure.

proof.title: You need to demonstrate the observed state
proof.body: Open State at date to assemble a verifiable reading for the relevant moment.

data.title: Understand how these data are established
data.lead: Origin, scope, calculations, freshness and limits — without interrupting the main reading.

origin.title: Origin
origin.body: The page brings together persisted business events, the audit journal, evaluation results, fleet state and operational probes. It does not manufacture a measure from the display alone.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: The period bounds eligible facts. A point in time adds a cut-off. The agent filter narrows only signals that can genuinely be attributed to that agent; the others remain global.

calculation.title: Calculation
calculation.body: Aggregates come from the backend or from simple, named compositions. Missing data are never silently replaced with zero.

freshness.title: Freshness
freshness.body: In the present, sources refresh according to their cost. In a past reading, automatic refresh stops and queries read the selected point in time.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Service state, some policy probes and the operator queue do not have a defensible history. They remain marked as current instead of being reconstructed artificially.

calculations.title: What the page actually calculates
calculations.lead: These rules explain the values most likely to raise questions.

fleet.title: Fleet total
fleet.body: Conversations observed for each agent are reconciled through their identity and attested transfers. A duplicate is removed only when that reconciliation can be established; otherwise the page states the uncertainty.

quality.title: Quality
quality.body: The share of evaluated turns rated satisfactory is compared with the objective returned alongside the measure. Without any evaluated turn, the page shows a dash rather than a false zero.

controls.title: Controls
controls.body: Counts include only controls with an available measure. In a past reading, rows remain in place but carry a dash when their data are missing.

risks.title: Open risks
risks.body: The indicator adds detected anomalies and triggered procedures. If both sources are unavailable, no value is asserted.

fleet.title: Fleet read
fleet.body: The /observability/fleet read receives the period and, when needed, the point in time. It returns per-agent measures and a reconciled bank total.

snapshot.title: Aggregated signals
snapshot.body: The /observability/snapshot read groups quality, cost, risk and conformity signals. The at and agent parameters are passed only to sources that can honour them.

time.title: Temporal contract
time.body: The URL carries the reading, period, point in time, comparison and agent scope. The cursor settles before sources are queried, avoiding one request per pixel.

live.title: Current-only legs
live.body: Service health, readiness, policy probes and the operator queue remain current. The rail also keeps a global timeline to support navigation.

validation.title: Validation
validation.body: Responses are bounded by FastAPI models and then checked by the BFF’s Zod schemas. A missing signal remains missing until it is honestly rendered as a dash.

closing.body: Overview tells you where to look. It becomes useful when you start with a gap, check its context, and then open the page that lets you understand, act, or prove.

viewAtlas.title: Choose the right lens
viewAtlas.lead: Each tab answers a different question. The view you came from is highlighted; the others remain explained so you can continue with confidence.

surfaces.signals: Tracks observed quality continuously, including targets, gaps, and measurement reliability.
surfaces.evaluations: Checks a candidate release against a governed case set before exposure.

signals.overview: Brings target, trend, coverage, and alerts together for the first reading.
signals.signals: Details each signal, its status, scope, and establishing source.

evaluations.cases: Describes the versioned case set: coverage, languages, categories, and expected requirements.
evaluations.runs: Shows each model’s result from one bench: the floor without a model, the thresholds, and the cases that decide.
evaluations.compare: Compares two campaigns on a constant scope so changes can be attributed correctly.
evaluations.archive: Lists every recorded execution, models and evaluation sets mixed, spanning months — the history, not the bench beside it.
evaluations.failed: Isolates the archive’s failing cases so their severity, cause and follow-up can be understood.
evaluations.models: Compares models across the whole archive; the bench gives a different figure, for different cases on a different date.
evaluations.judge: Measures the judge’s agreement with a hand-labelled set, and the disagreements that weaken any reading of the scores.

page.overview: Brings together protections, incidents, and gaps that warrant investigation.
page.promptInjection: Tracks attempts to divert instructions and how protections respond.
page.pii: Shows personal-data exposure risks and the controls applied to them.
page.guard: Explains guard decisions at the tool-call control point.
page.tools: Checks permissions, arguments, and refusals related to tools.
page.memory: Tracks memory persistence, scope, and erasure risks.
page.isolation: Checks separation between users, agents, and business contexts.
page.redteam: Presents executed adversarial scenarios and weaknesses that remain open.

page.overview: Summarises regulatory coverage, gaps, and available evidence.
page.mapping: Links regulatory frameworks to the controls and components supporting them.
page.obligations: Details each obligation, its status, and assigned responsibility.
page.evaluations: Shows assessed controls and results supporting the compliance reading.
page.incidents: Isolates events that may affect an obligation or commitment.
page.retention: Explains retention periods, due dates, and expected deletion.
page.evidence: Inventories supporting items and calls out missing evidence.
page.registry: Brings declared processing, purposes, and legal bases into one register.

page.overview: Combines availability, cost, performance, and capacity to guide diagnosis.
page.reliability: Tracks service continuity, errors, and reliability objectives.
page.cost: Breaks down usage and cost to reveal the main drivers.
page.performance: Shows latency, throughput, and degradation by service or model.
page.quotas: Tracks usage limits and remaining headroom before saturation.
page.incidents: Links interruptions and degradation to affected services.
page.capacity: Sets observed demand against available resources and limits.

page.overview: Summarises opportunities, expected impact, and improvement-cycle status.
page.plan: Orders selected improvements, owners, and next steps.
page.curation: Tracks cases proposed to strengthen evaluation sets.
page.experiments: Compares completed experiments, their hypotheses, and outcomes.
page.release: Connects a validated improvement to its release decision.

page.overview: Summarises open incidents, severity, and responses in progress.
page.incidents: Details each incident, scope, owner, and current state.
page.playbooks: Presents the response procedure planned for each type of situation.
page.orchestration: Shows response steps, dependencies, and approvals in sequence.
page.actions: Collects completed and pending actions with their traceable outcome.
page.postmortems: Keeps the resolved-incident analysis, causes, and accepted lessons.
page.problemes: Groups durable causes that may produce several incidents.
page.rapports: Prepares summaries for internal or regulatory follow-up.

page.overview: Summarises available captures, replays, and observed differences.
page.cassettes: Inventories captured exchanges that can be replayed without acting on a customer.
page.sessions: Groups captures by session to preserve end-to-end context.
page.shadow: Runs a candidate version in parallel without exposing its answer.
page.comparisons: Places reference and candidate side by side on the same inputs.
page.baselines: Defines the reference outcomes used to assess candidates.
page.diffs: Isolates differences in answer, tool use, cost, or decision.
page.evals: Connects replays to the evaluation verdicts that qualify them.
page.exports: Prepares shareable results without altering source evidence.

page.overview: Summarises candidates, coverage, and recent curation decisions.
page.curate: Presents cases to promote, review, or reject with context.
page.coverage: Shows languages, categories, and risks that remain under-covered.
page.promotions: Finds accepted cases and the evaluation set they strengthen.
page.rejections: Explains rejected cases and preserves the decision reason.
page.history: Traces curation decisions, authors, and effects.

page.overview: Summarises active rules, their activity, and items awaiting a decision.
page.rules: Describes each automation's conditions, actions, and safeguards.
page.executions: Traces observed triggers, outcomes, and errors.
page.approvals: Collects executions that require human approval.
page.audit: Preserves changes and decisions associated with automations.

page.overview: Summarises available evidence, integrity, and gaps to address.
page.evidencePacks: Groups the items needed for a given question or review.
page.exporters: Shows available outputs and export-destination status.
page.chain: Checks ordering, fingerprints, and possible breaks in the chain.
page.destinations: Tracks retention and delivery of evidence to authorised systems.

page.overview: Summarises active policies, changes, and expected approvals.
page.activePolicies: Presents the versions actually in force and their scope.
page.history: Traces versions, authors, approvals, and effective dates.
page.runtimeGuardrails: Links declared rules to protections applied during execution.
page.impactSimulator: Estimates the effects of a proposal before application.
page.approvals: Collects changes awaiting an authorised decision.

page.overview: Summarises sources, freshness, usage, and quality gaps.
page.sources: Inventories documents and systems available to agents.
page.memory: Shows memories, scope, lifetime, and consumers.
page.indexation: Tracks ingestion, chunking, and search-index status.
page.quality: Measures content coverage, freshness, and citability.
page.access: Explains which agents and roles may use each source.
page.retention: Presents retention periods, deadlines, and erasure rules.
page.history: Preserves source changes and ingestion operations.

page.overview: Summarises active settings and changes needing attention.
page.security: Presents settings governing access and protection.
page.data: Explains data retention, residency, and processing.
page.notifications: Chooses notified events and delivery channels.
page.integrations: Configures settings shared by connected services.
page.audit: Defines retention and use of administrative traces.
page.system: Exposes technical settings for platform operation.

sharedGuide.readingTitle: Read the page without getting lost
sharedGuide.actionTitle: What this page lets you do
sharedGuide.dataTitle: Understand how these data are established
sharedGuide.dataReadingRule: A value always describes a source, a scope, and a moment. If one is missing, the guide prefers an explained absence to misleading precision.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: Filters narrow only facts that can genuinely be attributed to them. A global signal remains global.

freshness.title: Freshness
freshness.body: Current data refresh according to cost; a past reading stops at the chosen time when the source can honour it.

examples.title: Concrete examples
examples.lead: These situations show how to move from displayed information to a defensible reading.

items.title: An agent appears inactive
items.body: Check the period and available sources first: no observed activity does not establish that the agent has stopped.

items.title: A queue is growing
items.body: Start with due date and status, then open the case or agent that actually carries the wait.

items.title: Two agents contribute to one journey
items.body: Use established identities and transfers before adding volumes or concluding that a duplicate exists.

items.title: The agent score drops
items.body: Link the run, failing cases, and served version before attributing the drop to the model.

items.title: A rule is declared active
items.body: Configuration says what should apply; execution traces show whether the rule was actually triggered.

items.title: A source is attached
items.body: Attachment permits use; only a citation or trace proves that it supported a specific answer.

items.title: An indicator deteriorates
items.body: Set period, scope, and comparison first, then trace the gap to the signal and agents that explain it.

items.title: The page shows a dash
items.body: The fact is not sufficiently established for this reading; replace it with neither zero nor the last known value.

items.title: An agent filter is active
items.body: Attributable facts narrow to that agent, while platform measurements remain explicitly global.

items.title: An action is proposed
items.body: Review the case, scope, and supporting evidence before approving an action on the current state.

items.title: You are reading a past date
items.body: The page can explain that state, but mutations remain frozen to avoid acting on an expired situation.

items.title: An automation fails
items.body: Separate the trigger, attempted action, and outcome before changing the rule.

items.title: An item is missing
items.body: The pack remains incomplete: exporting or presenting it differently cannot create absent evidence.

items.title: The chain is reported valid
items.body: Check order, fingerprints, and coverage up to the requested point, not only the latest item.

items.title: You must explain a past state
items.body: Choose the time and scope, then distinguish historised facts from facts available only now.

items.title: A new version is proposed
items.body: Compare it with the active version, identify affected consumers, and require the planned approvals.

items.title: A component is available
items.body: Catalogue presence proves neither immediate availability nor suitability for a business case.

items.title: A setting changes
items.body: Check scope and application mode: some changes require re-evaluation or redeployment.

items.title: A user has an account
items.body: The account establishes identity in the platform; roles still determine what the user may see or do.

items.title: A permission is removed
items.body: Check effective access after the change and preserve author, time, and justification.

items.title: The system appears operational
items.body: A current status guides diagnosis, but replaces neither a complete inventory nor certification.

operation.agents: Opening cases and changing assignments affect current state; the list remains a reading of the queue or fleet.
operation.agent: Tests, changes, and decisions remain attached to the selected agent; a past reading does not rewrite its current state.
operation.monitor: Monitoring pages are read surfaces. Their links lead to action surfaces without turning a signal into an automatic decision.
operation.act: Mutations apply only to current state, with authorisation, outcome, and author traceable. Past readings disable them.
operation.prove: Creating or exporting a pack does not change source facts; it assembles or delivers already established items.
operation.configure: A change follows the page's proposal and approval cycle. A stored value is not always effective immediately.
operation.admin: Identity and access changes apply now and must produce a usable administrative trace.

validation.body: The backend bounds responses, the BFF checks their shape, and rendering preserves absences instead of silently converting them into values.

body.agents: {page} helps find the right person, agent, or case before opening the detail needed for a decision.
body.agent: {page} explains one facet of the selected agent; its value comes from linking configuration, observed behaviour, and evidence.
body.monitor: {page} helps qualify a gap before action: which fact, over what scope, at what time, and with which limit.
body.act: {page} turns an observation into governed action without separating the decision from its context or trace.
body.prove: {page} helps demonstrate what can be established and makes missing items or periods visible.
body.configure: {page} shows the state actually declared, its impact, and the controlled path for changing it.
body.admin: {page} connects identity, authorisation, and system state so a change remains explainable and verifiable.

agents.title: Set the scope
agents.body: Start with the scope: the whole fleet, a work queue, or one specific agent.

agents.title: Prioritise
agents.body: Find the gap, status, or case that genuinely needs a decision.

agents.title: Follow through
agents.body: Open the related agent, evidence, or action instead of interpreting an isolated number.

agent.title: Confirm the agent
agent.body: The agent selector defines the scope of the whole page.

agent.title: Read the fact
agent.body: Distinguish what was observed, what was declared, and what remains unavailable.

agent.title: Connect the views
agent.body: Use cross-links to move from configuration to behaviour and then to evidence.

monitor.title: Set the reading
monitor.body: First choose the period, time mode, and scope that answer your question.

monitor.title: Spot the signal
monitor.body: Read the main signal, then its gap from the target or selected comparison.

monitor.title: Find the cause
monitor.body: Move down to the agents and events that explain the gap before acting.

act.title: Identify the case
act.body: Start with the case, version, or rule that is waiting for a decision.

act.title: Check the context
act.body: Review the related signals, tests, and evidence before taking action.

act.title: Act and record
act.body: Take the proposed action; its outcome and author must remain verifiable.

prove.title: Define the search
prove.body: Set the object, period, and scope of the evidence you need.

prove.title: Check the chain
prove.body: Check origin, integrity, and any gaps before reaching a conclusion.

prove.title: Keep or export
prove.body: Prepare a verifiable item without turning missing data into certainty.

configure.title: See what is active
configure.body: Start with the version or configuration that is actually in force.

configure.title: Measure the impact
configure.body: Find the agents, rules, and dependencies affected by a change.

configure.title: Change under control
configure.body: Use the proposal, approval, and traceability path provided by the page.

admin.title: Choose the scope
admin.body: Identify the person, role, or system component concerned.

admin.title: Check the real state
admin.body: Compare observed rights or state with what is expected.

admin.title: Apply with evidence
admin.body: Make the authorised change and verify that it leaves a usable record.

fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.lead: See the agents in the fleet and find the one that needs your attention.
fleet.question: Which agents are active, how is their work distributed, and where should you look next?
fleet.start: Start with the fleet overview, then open an agent only when a volume, status, or signal warrants investigation.
fleet.action: Choose the agent to examine and go directly to its summary, evaluations, or configuration.
fleet.data: The page joins the agent registry with the activity facts available for each agent.
fleet.limit: No activity does not prove that an agent is useless or stopped; it only describes what the sources observed in the displayed scope.

inbox.title: Needs attention
inbox.lead: Bring together approvals and blocked actions that need a human decision.
inbox.question: What cannot continue without an operator decision?
inbox.start: Start with urgency and deadline, then open the case to understand what is blocked and what evidence supports the request.
inbox.action: Approve, reject, or route the case to the right person while keeping the decision traceable.
inbox.data: The queue is built from operator items that are genuinely pending and their current state.
inbox.limit: The queue does not summarise every fleet risk; it only shows items explicitly waiting for intervention.

todo.title: To do
todo.lead: Find failed evaluation cases that need to be understood and corrected.
todo.question: Which evaluation failures require investigation or correction?
todo.start: Start with overdue or recurring cases, then read the failure cause before opening the affected agent.
todo.action: Assign the review, document the correction, and rerun the evaluation when the change is ready.
todo.data: The page reads failed evaluation cases and their handling state from the operator queue.
todo.limit: One failed case does not by itself establish that an agent is poor overall; it identifies a specific scenario to examine.

quality.title: AI quality
quality.lead: Track observed quality and the evaluations that precede release.
quality.question: Do answers meet the quality target, and are candidate versions ready?
quality.start: Choose between observed signals and evaluations, then start with the main gap before moving down to agents or cases.
quality.action: Open an agent’s evaluations, prioritise a correction, or inform a release decision.
quality.data: The reading combines observed quality signals and, in Evaluations view, the real results of evaluation runs.
quality.limit: An aggregate score does not replace failed cases or their coverage; a missing value remains missing evidence.

security.title: Security & privacy
security.lead: Understand attacks, personal data, access, and protections that were triggered.
security.question: Which exchanges met a security or privacy risk, and how were they handled?
security.start: Set the period and scope, then distinguish attempts, applied controls, and incidents that genuinely required action.
security.action: Isolate the agent or risk type to investigate, then open the related incident, rule, or evidence.
security.data: The page reads security, privacy, and control facts attached to observed exchanges.
security.limit: No signal means no fact was reported in this scope; it is not a security certification.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.lead: Read the regulatory posture from actions and controls that were actually observed.
compliance.question: Do agents follow the applicable obligations in the available facts?
compliance.start: Start with the obligation or domain that is off track, then examine the agents and facts that make up this reading.
compliance.action: Prioritise a check, open relevant evidence, or request a correction in the affected scope.
compliance.data: The posture is calculated from governance facts and controls attached to the obligations being tracked.
compliance.limit: This page provides an operational reading; it replaces neither legal advice nor a regulatory attestation.

reliability.title: Reliability & cost
reliability.lead: Track availability, response time, errors, and fleet consumption.
reliability.question: Is the service operating at the expected reliability and cost level?
reliability.start: Choose the period, find the availability, latency, error, or cost gap, then identify the contributing agent.
reliability.action: Open the responsible agent or incident and decide whether to diagnose, limit, or correct.
reliability.data: The page aggregates available service and usage facts for agents in scope.
reliability.limit: An average can hide a spike or an outlier agent; always read the distribution and period before concluding.

observability.title: Observability
observability.lead: Check the availability of Tessera, its dependencies, and its models.
observability.question: Is the technical chain required by the cockpit responding correctly?
observability.start: Start with the unavailable or degraded component, then read its latest check and affected dependencies.
observability.action: Route diagnosis to the right component and open the useful traces or procedures.
observability.data: The page reads health probes and technical states exposed by services and dependencies.
observability.limit: A green probe proves that one specific check responds at reading time; it does not guarantee that no other fault exists.

improvement.title: Improvement
improvement.lead: Choose useful corrections and measure their effect on agents.
improvement.question: Which gaps deserve improvement, and is an effect visible after correction?
improvement.start: Start with the largest gap, check its recurrence and agent, then compare the situation before and after the change.
improvement.action: Prioritise an improvement, link it to an owner, and check its effect in later signals.
improvement.data: The page joins available improvement signals, their priority, and observed changes.
improvement.limit: An improvement correlated in time does not by itself prove that the change caused it.

incidents.title: Incidents & procedures
incidents.lead: Track an incident, apply the right procedure, and verify its resolution.
incidents.question: Which incidents are open, which procedure applies, and how far has resolution progressed?
incidents.start: Start with severity and deadline, then open the incident to read the facts, procedure, and actions already taken.
incidents.action: Assign, apply a procedure step, escalate, or close with the expected evidence.
incidents.data: The page reads the incident register, events, procedures, and current state.
incidents.limit: Closure means the expected path was completed; it must not hide limitations or missing evidence.

replay.title: Replay & shadow test
replay.lead: Replay a session and test a candidate version without exposing it to customers.
replay.question: How would another version have behaved on an exchange already observed?
replay.start: Choose a captured session and a candidate version, then compare the result without confusing replay with live traffic.
replay.action: Document a gap, feed an evaluation set, or decide that a version still needs correction.
replay.data: Replay uses captured session elements and executes the candidate version within the intended scope.
replay.limit: A replay measures one captured scenario; it does not predict behaviour across all production traffic.

curation.title: Evaluation sets
curation.lead: Choose and enrich the exchanges used to evaluate agents.
curation.question: Do evaluation sets cover the cases that genuinely matter?
curation.start: Start with coverage gaps and cases to review, then check language, risk, and expected outcome.
curation.action: Accept, enrich, or discard a case to improve the next evaluation.
curation.data: The page reads candidate cases, their annotations, and their membership in evaluation sets.
curation.limit: A large number of cases does not ensure good coverage; diversity and expectation quality remain essential.

release.title: Release
release.lead: Check version, evaluations, and evidence before making an agent available.
release.question: Does each agent meet the observable conditions required for release?
release.start: Choose the agent, then read the evaluation verdict, candidate version, and required evidence together.
release.action: Approve, hold, or send a version back for evaluation while keeping the decision and reasons verifiable.
release.data: The page joins the evaluation seam, declared versions, and available release evidence.
release.limit: Ready describes configured and completed checks; it is not an absolute guarantee of future behaviour.

automations.title: Automated rules
automations.lead: Define what can run automatically and what remains subject to human approval.
automations.question: Which actions can trigger on their own, under what conditions, and with what control?
automations.start: Start with the active rule, its trigger, and authority level before reading its history.
automations.action: Propose, activate, suspend, or revise a rule through the expected approval path.
automations.data: The page reads declared automated rules, their state, and associated recorded executions.
automations.limit: An enabled rule does not claim that it was triggered; its execution must be confirmed by the journal.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.lead: Find sensitive actions and verify their traceability chain.
audit.question: Who did what, when, to which object, and does the chain remain verifiable?
audit.start: Set the period and object, then read the event, its author, and its integrity status.
audit.action: Reconstruct a decision, follow an incident, or open the associated evidence.
audit.data: The page reads audit log entries and verifies their chain using the cockpit’s integrity semantics.
audit.limit: The journal proves what was recorded in it; it cannot attest an event that never reached this seam.

evidence.title: Evidence centre
evidence.lead: Collect, verify, and export the elements that document what happened.
evidence.question: Which evidence exists for a given agent, period, or decision?
evidence.start: Start with the required scope, then check each item’s status, provenance, and integrity.
evidence.action: Assemble a pack, verify an item, or prepare an export for review.
evidence.data: The page reads the evidence store and metadata that link each item to its origin.
evidence.limit: A pack is complete only when expected items are present; an export fills no gap.

asof.title: State at a date
asof.lead: Reconstruct the known state of an agent at a chosen point in time.
asof.question: What did the system know and use at that precise time?
asof.start: Choose the agent and date, then distinguish truly historical elements from those still shown as current.
asof.action: Compare two states, explain a past decision, or prepare a point-in-time review.
asof.data: The page rebuilds state from available versions and events up to the selected time.
asof.limit: What was not historised cannot be reconstructed; the page must say so rather than silently reuse current state.

signals.title: Signal catalogue
signals.lead: Define each signal, its source, and the response expected when it changes.
signals.question: Which signals govern the cockpit, and what does each one mean?
signals.start: Find the signal, then read its definition, source, threshold, and expected response.
signals.action: Clarify or evolve a signal through the expected governance path.
signals.data: The page reads the declared signal catalogue and its governance metadata.
signals.limit: Declaring a signal does not prove that its source emits data; observation is checked on monitoring pages.

platformGuardrails.title: Guardrails
platformGuardrails.lead: See available protections and the agents to which they apply.
platformGuardrails.question: Which protections are active, and what scope do they cover?
platformGuardrails.start: Start with the rule and its mode, then check the agents using it and pending changes.
platformGuardrails.action: Prepare a protection change and identify the agents that will need reevaluation.
platformGuardrails.data: The page reads the platform guardrail catalogue and its declared consumers.
platformGuardrails.limit: A declared protection is not proof that it triggered; execution facts provide that evidence.

models.title: Models
models.lead: See available models and the agents using each one.
models.question: Which models are available and active, and which agents use them?
models.start: Start with the model actually being served, then check its consumers and planned changes.
models.action: Measure the impact of a model change and prepare reevaluation for affected agents.
models.data: The page reads the model catalogue and declared bindings to agents.
models.limit: A listed model demonstrates neither instant availability nor quality for a business case.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.lead: Understand the available connections between Tessera and external systems.
connectors.question: Which connectors exist, how are they configured, and do they respond?
connectors.start: Start with connector status, then read its configuration, scope, and latest check.
connectors.action: Configure, diagnose, or remove a connection under the expected rights and controls.
connectors.data: The page reads the connector registry, exposable configuration, and verification states.
connectors.limit: A declared or reachable connector does not prove that every business operation will succeed.

policies.title: Policies
policies.lead: Define platform rules and govern their changes.
policies.question: Which policies apply, and where is each change proposal in its lifecycle?
policies.start: Start with the active version, then compare the proposal, its scope, and required approvals.
policies.action: Propose, approve, reject, or trace a policy change.
policies.data: The page reads declared policies, versions, and governance history.
policies.limit: A written policy is not proof that it applied to an exchange; execution controls hold that evidence.

sources.title: Sources & memory
sources.lead: See the documents and memories on which agents can rely.
sources.question: Which sources feed agents, are they fresh, and where are they used?
sources.start: Start with the active source, then check freshness, coverage, and the agents consuming it.
sources.action: Attach, disable, refresh, or investigate a source according to its state.
sources.data: The page reads the source catalogue, ingestion states, and bindings to agents.
sources.limit: An available source does not prove it was used in a specific answer; a citation or trace must establish that.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.question: Which cross-platform settings are active, and what would a change affect?
parameters.start: Start with the current value and scope, then read the expected effect before changing it.
parameters.action: Update an authorised setting and verify that it is taken into account.
parameters.data: The page reads settings exposed by the platform and their currently stored values.
parameters.limit: A stored value is not always proof of immediate effect; some changes require reload or redeployment.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.lead: Connect and monitor external services integrated with Tessera.
integrations.question: Which integrations are active, configured, and correctly connected to the platform?
integrations.start: Start with integration state, then read its capabilities, configuration, and latest exchanges.
integrations.action: Configure, diagnose, or disable an integration through the expected path.
integrations.data: The page reads the integration registry and technical states exposed by each integration.
integrations.limit: An available global state does not guarantee every call succeeds or every received datum is valid.

users.title: Users
users.lead: Manage the people who can access Tessera and the state of their account.
users.question: Who has an account, in which state, and with which assignments?
users.start: Find the person, then check account state and assignments before opening their rights.
users.action: Create, update, suspend, or inspect an account according to your permissions.
users.data: The page reads the user registry and administrative attributes exposed by the platform.
users.limit: Having an account does not describe effective permissions by itself; check them in Roles & access.

roles.title: Roles & access
roles.lead: Manage roles, permissions, and effective access across the platform.
roles.question: Who can see or do what in Tessera, and why?
roles.start: Start with the role or user, then compare granted permissions with the actual need.
roles.action: Adjust an assignment or permission and verify its effect on the affected scope.
roles.data: The page joins identities, roles, and declared permissions to calculate visible access.
roles.limit: A rights matrix does not prove that an action occurred; the audit log carries that evidence.

systemProfile.title: System profile
systemProfile.lead: Read the environment’s technical configuration and operational state.
systemProfile.question: In which environment is Tessera running, and which components are genuinely active?
systemProfile.start: Start with environment and deployment mode, then check exposed models, dependencies, and states.
systemProfile.action: Route a diagnosis, confirm a configuration, or prepare a technical review.
systemProfile.data: The page reads exposable system configuration and operational states available at consultation time.
systemProfile.limit: This profile describes the observed environment; it replaces neither a full infrastructure inventory nor a certification.

settings.title: Personal settings
settings.lead: Adapt your experience without changing fleet governance.
settings.question: Which preferences apply to your use of the cockpit?
settings.start: Start with the preference you want to change and distinguish it from administrative platform settings.
settings.action: Change a personal preference and verify its effect in your session.
settings.data: The page reads preferences tied to your experience and the options your role may change.
settings.limit: A personal preference changes neither policies, agents, nor rights granted by administration.

agentSummary.title: Agent summary
agentSummary.lead: Bring together an agent’s identity, activity, performance, and alerts.
agentSummary.question: What does this agent do, what state is it in, and what should you inspect?
agentSummary.start: Confirm the selected agent, then start with the main alerts and indicators before opening details.
agentSummary.action: Choose the next analysis: configuration, test, evaluation, knowledge, or history.
agentSummary.data: The summary joins the agent’s declared record with available activity facts for the period.
agentSummary.limit: Some legs remain current when no history exists; the page must say so rather than simulate a past state.

agentConfigurations.title: Agent configurations
agentConfigurations.lead: View and govern an agent’s identity, model, behaviour, and status.
agentConfigurations.question: Which settings is this agent actually running with?
agentConfigurations.start: Start with the active value and its origin, then check changes and inheritance before editing.
agentConfigurations.action: Update an authorised setting or find the history of a configuration.
agentConfigurations.data: The page reads the agent’s declared configuration, availability, and available governed changes.
agentConfigurations.limit: At a past date, only historised elements can be read; the form and some states remain current.

agentKnowledge.title: Agent knowledge
agentKnowledge.lead: Understand the sources attached to this agent and their state.
agentKnowledge.question: Which sources can this agent rely on, and are they usable?
agentKnowledge.start: Start with active sources, then check coverage, freshness, language, and observed use.
agentKnowledge.action: Attach, disable, or investigate a source, then verify its use in answers.
agentKnowledge.data: The page reads sources attached to the agent and available usage or coverage indicators.
agentKnowledge.limit: Attaching a source does not prove it grounded a specific answer; the citation or trace must show that.

agentGuardrails.title: Agent guardrails
agentGuardrails.lead: See the rules and protections that constrain this agent’s answers.
agentGuardrails.question: Which protections apply to this agent, and in which mode?
agentGuardrails.start: Start with the active rule, severity, and mode, then read its origin and changes.
agentGuardrails.action: Prepare or review a protection change and connect the rule to observed controls.
agentGuardrails.data: The page reads guardrails attached to the agent and their declared configuration.
agentGuardrails.limit: An active rule does not prove it triggered; execution facts carry that evidence.

agentPrompts.title: Agent instructions
agentPrompts.lead: See active instructions, versions, and language coverage.
agentPrompts.question: Which instructions guide this agent, and which version is actually served?
agentPrompts.start: Start with the active snapshot, then check languages, variables, tests, and change proposals.
agentPrompts.action: Review an instruction, prepare a version, or open the evaluations that must validate it.
agentPrompts.data: The page reads the agent instruction catalogue, versions, and governed proposal cycle.
agentPrompts.limit: A declared instruction is not enough to explain an answer; the turn trace shows what was actually assembled.

agentBusiness.title: Agent business view
agentBusiness.lead: Read the business capabilities, signals, and runs genuinely attributed to this agent.
agentBusiness.question: Which business value does this agent produce, and under what level of control?
agentBusiness.start: Start with the main business signal, then move down to the capabilities and runs that compose it.
agentBusiness.action: Identify the capability to improve, run to review, or business control to strengthen.
agentBusiness.data: The page reads observed business facts attached to the agent’s declared capabilities.
agentBusiness.limit: An unattributed fact or insufficient observability remains absent; the page must not invent business value.

agentEvaluations.title: Agent evaluations
agentEvaluations.lead: Measure the agent’s answers and understand the verdict that precedes release.
agentEvaluations.question: On which cases does this agent pass or fail, and can it be made available?
agentEvaluations.start: Start with the verdict and selected run, then read failed cases, coverage, and languages.
agentEvaluations.action: Prioritise a correction, compare runs, or inform the release decision.
agentEvaluations.data: The page reads real evaluation runs, cases, scores, versions, and gate rules.
agentEvaluations.limit: A high score does not automatically compensate for a failed critical case or missing coverage.

agentConsole.title: Agent test console
agentConsole.lead: Test the agent and observe the sources, tools, and protections used on each turn.
agentConsole.question: How does this agent answer a specific case, and what happened during that turn?
agentConsole.start: Check the agent and sandbox settings, run a turn, then read answer, sources, tools, guardrails, and trace.
agentConsole.action: Understand a behaviour, export the trace, or send a useful case to evaluation.
agentConsole.data: The console combines the live turn with metadata and traces made available by the test seam.
agentConsole.limit: A console turn is a targeted test; it represents neither all production traffic nor a global verdict on the agent.

agentHistory.title: Agent history
agentHistory.lead: Find sessions, exchanges, quality, and compliance.
agentHistory.question: What happened in this agent’s sessions, and which ones deserve review?
agentHistory.start: Start with the period and sessions to watch, then open a session to read its turns and evidence.
agentHistory.action: Reconstruct a session, compare outcomes, or send a case to test and evaluation.
agentHistory.data: The page reads available sessions and transcripts for the agent, plus attached evaluations.
agentHistory.limit: A session that was not captured cannot be reconstructed; an available transcript does not imply it was evaluated.
